reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers and shares holiday matching, but consumers independently compose the occurrence policy.

duplication.why: Daily occurrence filtering and conditional weekend adjustment are repeated across shared scheduling and server consumers.

placement.why: Holiday predicates and date movement belong appropriately in shared/schedules.ts, but server handlers also own parts of the scheduling policy.

scope.why: The edits remain focused on the four scheduling requests and their supporting types, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Shared holiday matching is useful, but duplicated occurrence pipelines and independently chosen search limits make future rule changes harder to maintain consistently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange enumerate raw occurrences and reconstruct filtering and adjustment policy also owned by shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: Daily nonworking-day rejection appears as find in getNextWeekdayOccurrence, filter in getUpcomingDates, and continue in getDatesInRange; conditional date adjustment is similarly reshaped across consumers.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; getNextDate gains a daily-specific branch; getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange independently assemble occurrence policy instead of sharing that decision.
